basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 29.' and it opens 'VERS. 29.-- Duxerunt autem Abram et Nachor uxores. Nomen autem uxoris Abram Sarai, et'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 29.-- Duxerunt autem Abram et Nachor uxores. Nomen autem uxoris Abram Sarai, et nomen uxoris Nachor Melcha filia Aran, patris Melchae et patris Jeschae. Jescha ipsa est Sarai. Denique Aran filius Tharae frater Abram, et Nachor duas genuit filias: Melcham, et Sarai cognomento Jescham, e quibus Melcham | accepit uxorem Nachor, et Sarai Abram. Necdum quippe inter patruos, et fratrum filios nuptiae fuerant lege prohibitae, quae in primis hominibus etiam inter fratres et sorores initae sunt.
